description: Standard word list of RNL 0.4 (section 5.3 and Annex A of rnl-0.4.md); draft.

pseudo_kinds.name: owner
pseudo_kinds.meaning: `?` alone: in a symbol body, the object drawn with the symbol; in the body of a general definition, the usage being expanded (9.4)

pseudo_kinds.name: position
pseudo_kinds.meaning: the sub-object `::position` of an object (its origin)

pseudo_kinds.name: locatable
pseudo_kinds.meaning: an object with a position: instance, bundle, pin, terminal with a pin, point, text, the centre of a graphic written with a centre, a usage by its own point; a set given for it stands for each of its members (14.1)

pseudo_kinds.name: orientable
pseudo_kinds.meaning: an object with an orientation: instance, bundle, usage with a symbol

pseudo_kinds.name: constraint
pseudo_kinds.meaning: an object made by a constraint keyword

pseudo_kinds.name: set
pseudo_kinds.meaning: a set, written as a name; in ASSERT-TOPOLOGY also an item that is a `{…}` written out (15.4)

takes.name: one
takes.meaning: a single object; given a set, the keyword is applied to each member (5.2.1), except that PRIORITY takes a set marked with GROUP as the group itself (14.8)

takes.name: set
takes.meaning: a set; loose objects written for the slot form one set (5.2.1)

takes.name: any
takes.meaning: one object or a set, used as the keyword says (for DISTANCE, a set stands for each of its members, 14.5)

takes.name: shape
takes.meaning: a point, or a set of points (two forms of a graphic, 9.2.5)

takes.name: definition
takes.meaning: a definition: a `$` name, a `%` name bound to a definition, or an anonymous definition (5.6, 6.6)

keywords.summary: Declares the language version of the file.
Declares the name and version of a package.
Uses a package; with a body, an inline package. In the header record of a package file it references another package.
Declares another spelling for a standard word or a `$` name; with `definition=`, for a role, parameter or local name of that definition.
Loads an alias package.
Names the terminals of the instances that match by name, model or both, gives their type, or both; item by item, the later one counts.
Defines a symbol: graphics, pins and texts.

params.name: box
params.items: four numbers: x1, y1, x2, y2

keywords.summary: Defines a style from style properties, merging the styles in its braces.
Defines a general definition: a role list, a parameter list and a body.

params.name: roles
params.items: a role name, or [name, kind] where kind is a kind name or an array of kind names; "{name}" is a set role; the array may be empty

keywords.summary: A pin: a point of a symbol, which binds a terminal of an instance, a role of a usage, or nothing and is only drawn.

params.name: terminal
params.items: terminals; a non-empty array of them makes a bus pin (9.2.4)

keywords.summary: A line through two or more points.
An axis-aligned rectangle, by its centre and size or by two corners.
A circle, by its centre and radius or by its centre and a point on it.
An axis-aligned ellipse, by its centre and size or by two corners of its box.
An arc from the first point through the second to the third.
A cubic Bézier curve of 3n+1 points: the start point, then two control points and an end point for each segment.
A text: attached to a point it is an annotation, attached to an object a label.
keywords.key: attached object and key, when key is given
keywords.sentence: on #M1 there is a @TEXT("W/L = ${w}/${l}", key="wl", dy=-3)

keywords.summary: Puts the origin of an object at a point; one axis is enough.
Gives an object one of the eight orientations, or a pin one of four directions.

params.name: code
params.items: orientation codes, or the words left, down, right, up for R0, R90, R180, R270; for a pin, the direction it faces; a non-empty array of them makes one fact that holds when one of them holds (11.2)

keywords.summary: Puts an object on the bottom, middle or top drawing layer.
Gives an object a symbol; given to `#`, it is the block symbol of the subcircuit.

params.name: terminals
params.items: terminal names of the symbol, in the order of the nodes of the instance or of the role list of the usage; or pairs [terminal of the object or role name, terminal name of the symbol] (11.3)

keywords.summary: Gives an object a style.
Selects instances.
keywords.sentence: among the instances at each level in # and below, @SELECT-INSTANCE(model="nch", recursive=true) => they @SET-SYMBOL to $NMOS

keywords.summary: Selects terminals, with a pin or not.
keywords.sentence: among the terminals at each level in # and below, @SELECT-TERMINAL(net="vss", recursive=true) => they have @ASSERT-TERMINAL(same=["net"])

keywords.summary: Selects pins of drawn objects.
keywords.sentence: among the pins in # only, @SELECT-PIN(wired=false) => on them there is a @TEXT("${net}", key="netname")

keywords.summary: Selects nets.
keywords.sentence: among the nets at each level in # and below, @SELECT-NET(port=true, recursive=true) => $IO_PORT is @ATTACH to them

keywords.summary: Selects wires.
keywords.sentence: among the wires at each level in # and below, @SELECT-WIRE(bus=true, recursive=true) => they @SET-STYLE to $bus

keywords.summary: Selects labels.
keywords.sentence: among the labels at each level in # and below, @SELECT-LABEL(key="wl", recursive=true) => they @SET-STYLE to $grey

keywords.summary: Selects annotations.
keywords.sentence: among the annotations at each level in # and below, @SELECT-ANNOTATION(recursive=true) => they @SET-STYLE to $base

keywords.summary: Selects usages of a general definition, looking inward from the scope.
keywords.sentence: among the usages at each level in # and below, @SELECT-USAGE(recursive=true) of $DIFFERENTIAL_PAIR_N => they have @PRIORITY("disabled")

keywords.summary: Selects the usages that have the objects of the scope as members, looking outward.
keywords.sentence: among the usages containing #M1, @SELECT-ANCESTOR-USAGE of $DIFFERENTIAL_PAIR_N => named %dp_set

keywords.summary: Applies a general definition, written last, to the objects that fill its roles.
Applies a general definition, written first, to the objects that fill its roles.
A wire of a net (or of several nets: a bus) through two or more terminals or points.
Draws a whole net as wires: its pins are joined into a tree; the solver decides the branches and paths.
Joins the pins of some objects into a tree on each net that two or more of them share.
keywords.sentence: the pins of {#M1 #M2 #M5} are joined with @ROUTE-OBJECT

keywords.summary: Leaves the pins of a net out of the trees of ROUTE-NET and ROUTE-OBJECT.
Leaves the pins of some objects out of the trees of ROUTE-NET and ROUTE-OBJECT.
keywords.sentence: the pins of #M3 are left out with @UNROUTE-OBJECT

keywords.summary: Draws several host instances as one object.
Marks a set as a group, which the solver keeps together.
Adds objects to a named set.
Removes objects from a named set.
The union of sets, without duplicates.
Constraint: the members have the same coordinate on the axis.
Constraint: the members are in strict order in the direction.
Constraint: the members follow one another in the direction, in equal steps.
keywords.sentence: {#R1 #R2 #R3} are in @DISTRIBUTE("left-to-right"), i.e., in equal steps

keywords.summary: Constraint: the distance from the first object to the second in the direction.
Constraint: the orientation of the second object is that of the first followed by the transform; for two pins, their directions.

params.name: relation
params.items: orientation codes, not the words of ORIENT (11.2); a non-empty array of them makes one fact that holds when one of them holds (14.9)

keywords.sentence: from #M1 to #M2, they have @ORIENT-RELATION("MY"), i.e., flipped left-right

keywords.summary: Constraint: objects laid out as a table of nested sets, rows from top to bottom, each nested list at right angles; one group.
Settings of the solver, kept in the file or in the header record of a package; named parameters whose keys the solver defines, besides spacing_x, spacing_y and junction.
Changes the priority of a constraint or a usage, or turns a group on or off; a set with GROUP is taken as the group itself.
The direction of the current at a terminal.
Checks that the instances meet the conditions, have the attributes listed, and that the attributes listed are the same or different; only reports.
Checks that the terminals meet the conditions and that the attributes listed are the same or different; only reports.
Checks that the nets meet the conditions and that the attributes listed are the same or different; only reports.
Checks that the members are connected in series, in parallel, as a star or as a single loop; a usage or a set counts as a black box; only reports.

params.name: exclude
params.items: pairs [type, terminal]: the terminals of instances of that type that do not count

removed.what: value of direction of ORDER and DISTANCE
value of direction of ORDER and DISTANCE
condition of SELECT-TERMINAL, now of SELECT-PIN
